title: staggered-prefetch-allowance-merge-race-during-shard-eviction
creator: Alejandro Ruiz
description: Intermittent correctness bug in the rate-limiting policy engine observed during shard eviction and KV cache prefetch flows. Two asynchronous code paths (prefetch completion handler and eviction reconciliation job) can both apply allowance deltas to the same per-key ledger entry without robust idempotency, leading to either double-crediting or lost-credit depending on ordering. This manifests as transient throttling spikes for some orgs/routes and anomalous billing spikes for others.
reproduction_steps: Deploy runtime build with ENABLE_PREFETCH=true and run a simulated shard-migration using the dev shard-rebalance tool
Create a synthetic tenant with high short-burst traffic (50 reqs/s) against a single route with per-route burst pool enabled
Trigger a TTL-based KV cache eviction mid-burst by forcing a shard move with --force-evict flag
Observe allowance updates in the ledger by streaming internal-metering events from the dev metrics endpoint (http://dev-internal/metrics/ledger)
Repeat with different network latencies between shard manager and reconciler components to increase chance of interleaving
observed_behavior: Immediate ~2x allowance delta applied in logs for a small window (30-200ms) for certain keys
Downstream: 5-15s throttle spikes on affected routes followed by a burst of allowed requests once reconciler corrects ledger
Billing pipeline: sampled usage shows transient duplicate increments for some keys in the hourly rollup dashboard
SLO: per-route p99 latency increases during the throttle spike windows due to retry storms
expected_behavior: Allowance mutations for a single logical request or reconciliation event should be applied exactly once and be idempotent across concurrent reconciliation/prefetch/eviction flows. No transient double-credit or lost-credit should occur regardless of interleaving or network latency.
logs_snippet:
[2026-02-28T14:22:10.123Z] reconciler: apply_delta key=user:acct:42 delta=+120 trace=rek-3f2
[2026-02-28T14:22:10.150Z] prefetch-handler: commit_prefetch key=user:acct:42 delta=+120 trace=pref-98a
[2026-02-28T14:22:10.155Z] ledger: new_balance key=user:acct:42 balance=240 (expected 120)
[2026-02-28T14:22:15.001Z] throttler: throttle key=user:acct:42 route=/chat p99=512ms
hypothesis: Root cause: lack of a global idempotency token when separate components reconcile the same ledger row
Secondary: optimistic merge path in the fastpath writes a delta without checking an ongoing reconciliation marker, so two writers can both commit deltas
Tertiary: background reconciliation job does not currently use compare-and-swap semantics against a monotonic revision field for ledger rows
experiments_run: Added temporary fastpath guard (in-memory) to prevent two concurrent writers in the same process: reduced incidence in single-node tests
Injected artificial 50-200ms latency on reconciler RPCs: reproduced interleaving deterministically in perf lab
Implemented a patched compare-and-swap prototype using ledger.revision integer and ran 2k synthetic rebalances without duplicate deltas
immediate_mitigation: Enable conservative single-writer feature flag for shard-reconciler on affected clusters (flag: reconciler.single_writer=true)
Temporarily increase sampling of per-key meter events in production for suspect orgs to detect duplicates earlier
Notify SRE to monitor billing rollups and pause downstream auto-backfill for 1 hour windows if duplicate patterns spike
proposed_fix: Primary fix: make ledger updates transactional with a compare-and-swap on ledger.revision and attach an operation idempotency token for prefetch/reconcile operations
Add server-side idempotency store for short-lived reconcile op ids (TTL 60s) to reject duplicate commits
Hardening: extend unit+integration tests to include simulated shard failovers with injected RPC latency and verify ledger invariants
Add end-to-end regression test to the nightly canary harness that runs a deterministic shard move scenario and asserts no duplicate meter increments
rollout_plan: Merge change behind feature flag 'ledger.cas_reconcile' and run in dev/staging for 72 hours
Canary rollout to 5% of edge clusters with high-traffic test tenants and increased ledger sampling
If no duplicates observed after 48 hours, expand to 50% then to 100% over a week
Post-rollout: run billing reconciliation job and compare hourly aggregates to baseline for first 24 hours
acceptance_criteria: No duplicate allowance increments for test scenarios covering >10k shard moves in staging
Billing rollups show <=0.1% variance vs baseline after fix when exercising synthetic bursts
E2E regression in nightly canary shows zero occurrences of the prefetch/reconcile interleaving assertion
Code review signoff from runtime, metering, and SRE teams
